description.purpose: One screen, reached at /<mount>/ on the colony's one listener, that many agents and applications write onto at once. A view is a named, owned, optionally expiring piece of that screen: whoever sends one owns it, replaces it under the same name, and takes it down again. A store holds what is up, a code cell keeps that set and the display's object tree in agreement, and a display cell serves the page. Since 1.0.2 a `key` collision inside a component tree is a named refusal on `receipt` rather than a node that quietly disappears, and a key that is a plain number is refused with it. Since 1.1.0 the screen has two columns: `main`, wide, and `aside`, narrow, for the widgets that stand there whether or not anybody is talking -- and the order inside a column is the `ord` a view declared, then first appearance, never the last write. Since 2.0.0 the screen has no port of its own: the `web` cell it holds hangs on the colony's one listener under `override_params.web.mount` (`display` as shipped), so one reverse-proxy rule in front of that listener covers the whole colony. Since 1.2.0 the screen carries a microphone: a hold-to-talk button that joins a `voice:<call>` topic on the page's own socket, so the person looking at the screen can speak to the colony and hear it, provided a `voice` cell is mounted under the name the display was given (`voice_mount`, default `voice`). Since 2.0.1 that button says what it is doing while the browser asks for the microphone, tells a person to press again when the answer came after they let go, and treats a closed call as the end of a call rather than the end of the button: the next press joins again, and only a refused join is final. Since 2.1.0 the screen brings its own design language: the sheet and a catalogue of twenty-six components -- four windows and twenty-two pieces of content -- travel inside the `display-shell` definition, so an application names `display-pane` or `display-clock` in its tree and defines only what is its own. A screen recognises its own outdated vocabulary: the root carries a fingerprint of the definitions, and a running screen whose root holds another one gets the whole list defined again on its next pass, once. The faces are an operator asset with an empty default: `params.font_base` names the directory the two font files are served from, empty means no `@font-face` and the fallback stacks carry the type, and no font file ships in this repository. Since 2.2.0 the screen curates what it shows: every window carries a context and a relevance as hints, the root carries a focus number and per-context weights, the compose cell scores each window, hides what falls below the bar, gives exactly one window in `main` the focus rung, lets a window leave over two frames, and a title's presence follows the rung. A `timer` cell strikes at the moment the compose cell predicts, an `llm` cell may re-judge the whole screen on a content change, and a classified notice arrives on `in_notice`. Since 2.2.1 a hold survives the button moving under the pointer: the press captures the pointer, the state line has a height before it speaks, and a page that loses focus or goes hidden releases. Since 2.2.2 an application says `touched` (an epoch, as text) on a window whose content is new -- the screen compares a window's own props, and an answer in a child component is invisible to that comparison unless the application says so -- and the hold-to-talk button is a fixed point on the screen with its two lines floating above it. Since 2.2.3 a pass that computes the moment already ordered from the clock orders the same second again without removing it first, and the clock treats a repeated order as one order -- before, the re-add collided with the row the remove had just marked, and the moment never struck.
description.use_when: A person should be able to look at what several agents and applications are doing, in one browser tab, without those agents knowing about each other or about HTML. One screen is one instance under one mount: a second screen is a second instance under a second name, and the page is at /<mount>/ on the colony's listener.
description.not_in_scope: Not a window manager -- nothing overlaps, nothing has a z-order, nothing is resized, and there is no camera. A judgement of relevance rather than of layout: two regions and an order -- the `ord` a view declared, then its first appearance, ties broken on identity, and never the moment a view was last written. It never invents content and never edits it -- an application brings its own components and its own tree, and this scope only wraps, places and removes them. Since 2.2.0 the compose cell is not the model: it is deterministic and offline, the `judge` beside it is the one cell that asks a provider, and the screen stands complete without it. No authentication and no TLS (R-W8-2): since 2.0.0 the display binds nothing at all, and whatever stands in front of the colony's one listener is the whole access story. No interior address either -- `params.ports` is empty, so a caller names the hive and a lane (in_view, in_withdraw and in_notice in, event and receipt out).
examples: an assistant sends in_view {view_id: 'today', kind: 'prose', content: {title: 'Today', body: '...'}, ttl_ms: 3600000} -- a card appears, and stops being drawn an hour later

an application sends in_view {view_id: 'colony-view', kind: 'component', components: [{name: 'colony-view-node', ...}], content: {component: 'colony-view-node', props: {...}, key: 'n.os~builder', keep: ['hand','pinned']}} -- it brings its own vocabulary and its own tree
a person clicks something on that tree -- the event leaves the hive carrying the owner and view_id it belongs to, and the member routes it back to the one agent that put the view up

an application sends in_view {view_id: 'ambient', region: 'aside', ord: -10, kind: 'component', ...} -- a clock, a weather tile and a countdown stand in the narrow column beside the conversation, and rewriting them every twenty seconds moves nothing on the page

a person holds the button on the screen and speaks -- the frames reach the `voice` cell over the socket the page already holds, the transcript appears on the button's own line, and the answer is played back through it
